verdicts.strongest_argument: Every input is wire copy. The $17.02/carton Q3 FY25 comp was in the September 2025 release; the '$20+/carton and about $1/carton a month between now and October' quote is in the 9 June call transcript and was picked up in the reporting summaries ('buoyed by lemon prices exceeding $20 per carton'); and the Sunkist volume shift into H2 is not an inference at all - the 9 June press release states in terms that the company expects H2 to be its seasonally strongest period with Q3/Q4 benefiting from higher lemon volumes under the Sunkist agreement. What is genuinely new is only the subtraction ($132.13M less $42.1M = $90.0M against H2 FY25's $90.3M), which is mechanical and rests on a three-analyst S&P Global consensus that is a weak statement of what a $270M microcap's marginal holder expects. The tape suggests the market has already credited the recovery: the stock is 17% above the $12.85 of the 2 June Groundbreaker thesis, +7.65% over 20 days and only 4.26% off its 52-week high, with call-heavy open interest (P/C 0.67). The finding also omits the half of the comp that cuts the other way - Q4 FY25 realised $23.33/carton, above management's current $20+, so the favourable price lap exists in Q3 and reverses in Q4, which is exactly why a flat H2 consensus is defensible rather than lazy.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Q2 FY26 release gives H1 revenue $42.1M vs $69.4M, Q2 cartons 1,028,000 at $16.63, and states H2 is expected to be the seasonally strongest period on higher Sunkist lemon volumes.
CEO Edwards: pricing above $20/carton, strongest since 2018, average going up about $1 a carton each month between now and October.
Full-year lemon guidance reiterated, avocado guidance raised, H2 framed as seasonally strongest.
FY25 total net revenue $159.7M (so H2 FY25 = $90.3M) and Q4 FY25 fresh lemon price of $23.33/carton.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: +7.65% 20d and +5.98% 5d run-up into the print, spot 15.06 only 4.26% below the 52-week high and 27.3% above the low; last print reacted +8.93%. Open interest is call-tilted (put/call 0.67) on 382 contracts. The direction of the run-up is the direction of this claim, which is agreement rather than information - though the 382-contract, 48%-spread option book means the options say almost nothing.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that the $132.13M FY26 consensus was refreshed after 9 June by at least two of the three analysts and still implies flat H2 - that would turn a possibly-stale number into a real statement of expectations and drop this toward 30.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The arithmetic is right but the framing overstates it, and every number in it is in the wire copy of two press releases. The 4.0-4.5M carton guide and the 681,000 / 1,028,000 H1 splits are in the Q1 and Q2 FY26 releases; the 1,397,000 and 821,000 H2 FY25 comparatives are in the Q3 and Q4 FY25 releases. Subtracting H1 from a reiterated full-year guide is the first thing any of the three covering models does. More damaging: the low end of the range needs H2 of 2,291,000 against 2,218,000 last year - up 3.3%, which is precisely the modest step-up management attributed to the Sunkist cadence shift. Only the 4.5M top end requires the ~1.9M Q4 the finding calls impossible, and guiding to a range whose top is a stretch is not a surprise, it is what a range is for. On a name where the last four prints moved on impairments, asset sales and EBITDA, printing 4.1M instead of 4.5M cartons is not the swing factor. And this is the number that gets published tonight - reading it off the guide two hours early is not an edge over the tape.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Reiterates FY2026 fresh lemon volume guidance of 4.0-4.5 million cartons and reports Q2 volume of 1,028,000 cartons at $16.63.
Management reaffirmed 4.0-4.5M cartons despite the weak Q2, attributing the shortfall to Sunkist seasonal cadence pushing volume into Q3/Q4; no analyst challenged the feasibility in Q&A.
Q3 FY25 release: approximately 1,397,000 cartons at $17.02 average price - the comparative the finding uses.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: None supporting a downside surprise: the tape is up 7.65% over 20 days into the print and sits near the 52-week high, and open interest is call-tilted. If a guidance shortfall of this size were feared the run-up and the P/C ratio would both point the other way.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Independent third-party California lemon shipment or Sunkist volume data for May-July 2026 showing Q3 tracking below roughly 1.3M cartons - i.e. a miss against even the low end - would make this a real unpriced negative and take it under 25.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The load-bearing sentence is misread, and the misreading inverts it. The December 2025 amendment does not make the covenant resume at 31 October 2026 - it defers the 31 October 2026 measurement. The 10-Q language is 'defer measurement as of October 31, 2026 and resume a debt service coverage ratio of 1.25:1.0 measured as of October 31, 2027 and for any fiscal year ending thereafter', and the underlying 8-K exhibit 10.1 states the minimum DSCR as 'greater than or equal to 1.25:1 for the fiscal year ending October 31, 2027'. The total net leverage covenant is likewise deferred through 31 July 2027. So there is no test six weeks after this fiscal year end; the amendment removed exactly the risk the finding describes, and it did so nine months ago. Everything else in the finding - H1 adjusted EBITDA of about -$9.5M, total debt $94.1M, cash $891k, revolver headroom - is in the 9 June 10-Q and release and was covered the same day (TipRanks, 'Limoneira Bets on Asset Monetization After Tough Quarter'), and the covenant was already singled out as 'the near-term constraint' in a public 2 June thesis piece. Since then the position has improved in public: Windfall Farms was auctioned on 17 August for $15M all cash closing 14 September, against the $10M cash plus $6M seller note management had guided on the June call.

prior_publication.what_it_says: AgWest amendment sets the minimum DSCR at 1.25:1 for the fiscal year ending October 31, 2027 and thereafter, and net leverage at 4.50:1 from the quarter ending October 31, 2027 - not October 2026.
10-Q states the lender deferred the October 31, 2026 DSCR measurement and resumes 1.25:1.0 measured as of October 31, 2027, alongside the debt, cash and EBITDA figures the finding quotes.
Same-day coverage of the weak quarter and the asset-monetisation/deleveraging response.
Public long thesis that explicitly flags rising net debt, negative operating cash flow and the debt-service-coverage covenant as the near-term constraint.
Windfall Farms Paso Robles vineyard sold at public auction for $15 million all cash, closing expected 14 September 2026.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The stock rose into and after the 17 August asset-sale news (+7.65% over 20 days, +5.98% over 5) and trades near its 52-week high - the opposite of a market pricing a covenant breach six weeks out. Nothing in the option book (382 contracts, no usable skew) shows paid-for downside.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A subsequent amendment or a 10-Q/8-K showing the October 31, 2026 DSCR measurement was reinstated, or a going-concern-flavoured disclosure in tonight's filing, would make the mechanism real and take this to the 20s.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Both halves are published; only the join is not. The Interior Record of Decision of 21 August was a heavily covered national story - Navajo Times, azfamily, KNAU, Western Water all carried the 1.25 maf Lower Basin cut and Arizona's 760,000 acre-feet on the day - so it is not an obscure document. And the Limoneira side is squarely in the wire copy: the April 2026 decision to cease citrus on the last 600 Yuma acres 'to monetize Class 3 Colorado River water rights by conserving water', the 9 June release's statement that the company 'anticipates a monetization event from its Colorado River water rights in fiscal year 2026', and the CFO's call comment naming the 31 December 2026 contract expiries as the trigger. A public long thesis on 2 June had already valued the water at $50-70M of catalyst. The dated catalyst was therefore in investors' hands three months before the ROD. Two further discounts: the ROD's mandatory Arizona reduction falls overwhelmingly on priority-4 CAP rather than on priority-3 on-river districts like Yuma Mesa, so the paying channel is the voluntary 700,000 acre-feet conservation tranche rather than the mandatory cut - 'the gate opened' is softer than stated; and the ROD changes nothing in the May-July quarter being reported, so it reaches tonight only as call commentary. Against that, I concede the specific join - that the federal precondition for the company's own stated FY26 monetisation cleared 19 days before this print - appears nowhere I could find, and no 8-K has announced a Colorado River deal (the only monetisation press release, $30,000/acre-foot, was Santa Paula Basin in January 2025). That is why this is the least-priced of the four.

prior_publication.what_it_says: States the company anticipates a monetization event from its Colorado River water rights in fiscal year 2026 and that it ceased citrus farming on 600 Yuma acres in April 2026 to monetize Class 3 rights.
CFO Hamm ties monetisation timing to Colorado River contract expiries on 31 December 2026 and describes long-term lease or sale of access rights freed by crop substitution.
Same-day national coverage of the ROD: 1.25 maf Lower Basin cut with Arizona 760,000, California 440,000, Nevada 50,000 acre-feet.
Burgum signed the 2027-2028 operating guidelines and post-2026 ROD on 21 August, including an additional 700,000 acre-feet of voluntary Lower Basin conservation.
Public thesis valuing LMNR's ~21,000 acre-feet at $100M base and naming water monetisation of $50-70M as the lead catalyst.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The ROD (21 August) falls inside the 20-day run-up window, which is +7.65% - but the 17 August Windfall Farms auction at $15M all cash is the more natural explanation for that move, and the +5.98% 5-day leg post-dates both. Spot 4.26% below the 52-week high with call-tilted OI is consistent with some, not all, of a water catalyst being anticipated. I cannot separate the two events with 61,843 shares a day of volume.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Any article, note or press mention between 21 August and today linking the post-2026 ROD to Limoneira's Yuma Class 3 rights would push this to 75; conversely, confirmation that priority-3 Yuma Mesa water is eligible for a funded post-2026 conservation agreement at a disclosed price would take it under 25.

interactions: Three of the four rest on the same two documents filed together on 2026-06-09 (the Q2 8-K exhibit 99.1 and the 10-Q for the period ended 2026-04-30), so their independence is largely illusory. #0 and #1 are direct mirrors drawn from the identical carton/price table: #0 argues the sell side gives no credit to the Sunkist volume shift into H2 and is therefore too low, while #1 argues the H2 volume implied by that same shift is arithmetically unreachable. They cannot both be right and they point opposite ways; scoring both at full weight is one table counted twice with the sign flipped. #1 and #2 also share the same filing pair. #2 and #3 rest on the same balance sheet and the same 31 October 2026 fiscal year end - if the Colorado River monetisation in #3 lands, the liquidity strain in #2 is relieved by the same cash, so the two sizes are not additive; and #2's premise is in any case a misreading, since the December 2025 amendment defers rather than reinstates the October 2026 DSCR test. Finally, the Windfall Farms auction (17 August, $15M all cash versus the $10M cash plus $6M note guided in June) is a public, favourable development that cuts against #2 and shares the run-up window with #3's ROD, and no finding accounts for it.
